steps.body: After the sort, count each group: touch and count the reds, then the blues. Each group earns its own number.
steps.narration: After the sort, count each group: touch and count the reds, then the blues. Each group earns its own number.

widget.prompt: Build the whole after a color sort: 3 red buttons are shown. Add 4 blue buttons to make 7 altogether.

commonCounts.feedback: 3 leaves 4 dots still missing. Continue until the frame shows exactly 7.
6 leaves 1 dot still missing. Continue until the frame shows exactly 7.
8 adds 1 too many. Remove the extra so the frame shows exactly 7.

widget.missFeedback: Both colors count: the 3 red already there plus your blue must total 7.
widget.successFeedback: 3 red and 4 blue — 7 altogether; the sort's groups add up to the whole.

predict.prompt: Two sorted color groups fill one frame. The frame's total is…
predict.reveal: The whole is its parts together — the sort split the total, and the counts rebuild it; just the bigger group would leave the smaller group's buttons out of the total.

cml.actionGoal: Compare fairly — same start line, level seesaw, one sorting rule — for kmd count categories.
invariants: Fair comparison has fixed rules: lengths compare from one same start line, weights compare by which pan sinks, and sorted groups compare by their counts — the anchors for kmd count categories.
misconceptions: Judging length before aligning starts, reading size as weight, or comparing groups by how much space they fill instead of their counts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the starts were not lined up, could the far ends still settle which is longer?

widget.prompt: Start at 5 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 7 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 8.
9 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 5 to land on 8.

widget.missFeedback: Count 3 on from 5: you land on 8.
widget.successFeedback: 5 shapes and 3 more make 8 — counting finishes what sorting starts.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts are needed to reach 8.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 3 numbers, on 8.

widget.prompt: After sorting shapes into groups, what does counting each group add?

options.label: Nothing — sorting was enough
options.feedback: The sort already makes meaningful groups; counts add sizes that you can compare.

options.label: It undoes the sort
options.feedback: Counting keeps the sort in place and adds a number to each group.

options.label: Bigger shapes count double
options.feedback: Each shape is one member; size never changes a count.

options.label: A number for each group, ready to compare
options.feedback: Correct — sorting builds the groups, counting names their sizes, comparing crowns the largest.
